Virtual Resection is a technique for selectively suppressing portions of a volume dataset to resolve occlusion problems, particularly in medical imaging where internal structures (e.g., pulmonary nodules) are hidden by surrounding tissue (e.g., lung parenchyma) [S2].

The claim states that Virtual Resection is a technique for selectively suppressing portions of a volume dataset to resolve occlusion problems, particularly in medical imaging where internal structures (e.g., pulmonary nodules) are hidden by surrounding tissue (e.g., lung parenchyma). Source [S2] explicitly describes a computational framework to solve the occlusion problem between lungs and pulmonary nodules in chest CT images by selectively cutting lung tissue around nodules. It details how voxels inside a closed curve (except for the nodule itself) are cut off to solve the occlusion problem. The source confirms the use of volume clipping (virtual resection) to hide surrounding tissue (lungs) to reveal internal structures (nodules).
